delegate.summary:
I added 12 regression tests in a new Describe 'Capacity telemetry regressions', placed inside the outer 'aos isolated suite' right after 'Vendor capacity (R34)'. tests/aos.Tests.ps1 is the only file changed: 206 lines added, 0 removed, so no existing test was edited. The new block is ASCII-only. Each test sets AOS_COORD and CODEX_HOME to throwaway folders under $TestDrive and puts CODEX_HOME back afterwards, so nothing touches the real ~/.codex, the profile or the network. aos.psm1 is unchanged.

I ran the full suite once under PowerShell 7 with tests/Run-Tests.ps1. It exited 1 with 426 passed and 12 failed. The 12 failures are exactly the 12 new tests; every existing test, including the 8 'Vendor capacity (R34)' tests, passed. Here is why each new test fails today:
1. Windows on a reported event: expected 15 left, got 60. The function quietly ignores -Windows (it ends up in $args), so the weekly window never binds.
2. Every logged Codex window has passed: expected state 'reset', got 'ok'. Today a passed reset is counted as a fresh 100 %.
3. Codex reading older than 5 h with its resets still ahead: expected 'stale', got 'ok'.
4. Codex reading timestamped 10 minutes in the future: expected 'unknown', got 'ok'.
5. Malformed window (150 % used): expected 80 left on the week window, got -50. The bad window is used to decide capacity instead of being excluded.
6. Read-AosCodexLimits with a missing or zero resets_at: it returns 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z as the reset.
7. Old ledger row without windows: still read correctly, but the result has no 'windows' property.
8. `aos capacity set ... --weekly/--weekly-resets`: throws 'unknown or incomplete option: --weekly'.
9. Malformed CLI input: `--resets 25:00` throws a TimeSpan.Parse exception instead of printing usage. This test also covers `--resets garbage`, a lone `--weekly`, a lone `--weekly-resets`, and bad weekly values.
10. `aos capacity --json`: prints nothing on stdout, only the usage warning, so there is no JSON.
11. Text output under the th-TH culture: the ISO time given to `--resets` is stored as year 3112 instead of 2026. This is a real bug today, not just a missing feature.
12. Get-AosCapacityWarning for a reset, stale or future Codex reading: returns $null instead of a message telling you to refresh.

Assumptions the tests make where the contract leaves details open:
- The state names are 'reset', 'stale' and 'unknown'.
- Window labels are '5h' and 'week'.
- -Windows items are objects with label, used (percent used) and resets (ISO UTC).
- Each window carries its own .state.
- The text output contains the word 'reset' and the reset time as HH:mm, in either local time or UTC; an unknown reset shows the word 'unknown'.
- The warning text contains 'refresh'.
- The JSON is either an array of vendor objects or an object keyed by vendor.

Possible conflict for the implementer: the existing test 'ignores a malformed capacity row' expects no warning for a ledger row whose reset is 'not a date'. If the fix marks such rows 'unknown' and warns on 'unknown', that existing test will break.
unverified: Windows PowerShell 5.1 run of tests/Run-Tests.ps1: blocked because the command needed approval in this session, so I don't know how the new tests behave under 5.1. One risk: the th-TH culture switch in the text-output test may not take effect under 5.1.
`aos test` (both shells plus the parse and ASCII checks) was not run as a whole. I checked separately that the new block is ASCII-only.
A filtered run of only the capacity Describes was blocked by the command validator; I ran the full suite instead.
That these tests pass once the fix exists: they can't go green until the production change is made.

task:
Write independent regression tests only for the capacity reporting improvement in the current plan. Only edit tests/aos.Tests.ps1, preserve all existing tests unchanged. Use your isolated delegate worktree and disposable fixtures; no profile/network writes. New Describe 'Capacity telemetry regressions' inside the existing outer Describe. Tests should expose real pre-fix behavior, not mirror implementation. Verify the new tests fail for the intended reasons and report each failure; no production changes.
Contract: Add-AosCapacityEvent gains optional Windows (array objects label, used, resets) and existing callers work. Get-AosCapacity includes windows retaining individual state, never invents fresh100% after a reset; when all log windows have passed state=reset, remaining=null. Fresh live weekly window continues to bind after session reset (existing test untouched). Log older than5h with future reset is stale, future observation beyond60sec is unknown. Missing/zero resets_at or out-of-range used_percent => malformed window excluded from availability; no throw. Unknown stays unknown; no epoch reset implying full. Read-AosCodexLimits is tested via disposable CODEX_HOME. Existing old ledger capacity event without Windows remains compatible. CLI adds --weekly <percent-left> and --weekly-resets <ISO> as a paired option to capacity set, records both windows (5h/week); malformed reset25:00/garbage or incomplete weekly pair gives usage, writes no event and does not throw. CLI `aos capacity --json` outputs valid JSON with explicit depth, ISO UTC string reported and reset dates, windows/source/state and null remaining when reset/unknown. Text output includes reported resets (or explicit unknown), window and observation/source. Dates are culture independent. Get-AosCapacityWarning warns to refresh reset/stale/unknown observations without stopping a delegation. Keep test count bounded (about10-14 tests). Do not require future new features outside this contract. No existing test rewrites. Return tests and red evidence, not fixes.
